newsitem.title: HONG KONG: The worst Hong Kong fires on record.
newsitem.headline: The worst Hong Kong fires on record.

text.p: Worst fires on receord in Hong Kong.

1918 - In the worst fire on record, an estimated 600 people were killed and 400 injured at the Happy Valley racecourse on Hong Kong Island on the Lunar New Year holiday when a matshed grandstand collapsed and food stall stoves were knocked over, setting bamboo matting ablaze.
1929 - A blaze in the Prince Edward Hotel in Hong Kong's Island's Central district kills nine people
1947 - The Canton steamer S.S. Sai On was consumed by fire on the Hong Kong dockside, killing 149 people.

1953 - On Christmas Day, the Shek Pik Mei squatter village burned down, making more than 60,000 homeless. There were no records of the exact numbers living there and the death toll is unknown. As a result of the fire Hong Kong launched a drive to eliminate squatting by building cheap public housing, in which 3.5 million people now live.
1971 - Fire sweeps through Jumbo Restaurant in Aberdeen harbour , killing 13 and injuring 42.
1972 - The cruise liner Queen Elizabeth, which was being used as a floating university, burned and sank in Hong Kong harbour, with no casualties.
1981 - Fire at a wig factory in North Point kills 11 workers.
1984 - Blaze rages through the Blue Box Industrial Building in Hing Wo Street, injuring 44.
1986 - Fire guts Chu Ku Tsai village on Chinese Lunar New Year holiday, leaving 2,000 homeless.
1986 - Fourteen people were killed in a blaze at a garment factory in the Kwai Chung port district.
1986 - A Christmas blaze guts 150 vessels moored in Aberdeen typhoon shelter on Hong Kong Island, leaving over 1,700 boat dwellers homeless and virtually penniless. But only two injured.
1990 - Triad gangsters fire-bomb a restaurant and majong parlour in Hunghom, killing six and injuring 24.
1990 - Six dead and 50 injured in a fire in a "cage home" slum hostel in Shamshuipo.
1992 - A blaze at the Shek Kong Vietnamese refugee detention centre killed 26 and injured 126.
1994 - A fire-bomb at the Shek Pik Mei branch of a Hong Kong bank killed 12 bank employees.
1996 - A February dry season brush fire traps schoolchildren hiking at Pat Sin Leng in the New Territories. Three pupils and two teachers killed, many suffer life-lasting burn injuries.

1996 - On November 20 the Garley Building in Kowloon's Nathan Road tourist shopping street turns into a towering inferno, killing 39 people and injuring 81. It was the worst blaze in a building on record in the British colony.
1997 - On January 25 a blaze in a karaoke bar killed 15 people in the Tsimshatsui red light district. Police suspect arson.
